clue.text: One striped by this kind of punishment?

definitions.text: One striped by this kind of punishment?

parts.words: One striped by this kind of punishment?
parts.note: an NCO wears two stripes on the sleeve, and the same word names punishment of the body, such as a striping with the cane

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that 'striped' means both wearing rank stripes and being striped by a cane; the same word names the rank and the beating.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-commissioned rank wears two chevrons, and physical punishment such as caning goes by the same adjective.

clue.text: Paramour' doesn't begin to understand royal master

indicators.note: the word for paramour does not start, so its opening letter goes

parts.note: a lover is a paramour
to see is to understand, as in I see

explanation.surface: A lover is baffled by a king who rules him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't begin' cuts L from LOVER, leaving OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor or boss in charge of workers is their master.

clue.text: Star's movement a valid subject for debate?

explanation.definitionFit: In astronomy a star's apparent drift across the sky has this name; at a meeting, a correctly framed resolution to debate.

clue.text: One who may try a pipe

explanation.definitionFit: A part-time judge in English courts who tries cases has this title; it is also a simple wooden flute.

clue.text: Bound to put a few coins in the hat

indicators.note: the coins are put in, so they go inside the word for hat

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
a mite is a small coin and a small contribution, as in the widow's mite

explanation.surface: Someone feels obliged to toss some small change into the collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like a leap or a duty; it is the adjective meaning restricted. The widow's mite is the Bible's tiny gift of coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bound or restricted is kept within limits.

clue.text: Dancing master selected pupils

indicators.note: dancing moves around, so the letters of master are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dancing teacher picked the best students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancing' rearranges MASTER. A stream is a school group of pupils of similar ability.
explanation.definitionFit: In schools a group of children chosen by ability is put in a set or band of this name.

clue.text: A delay upset this celebration

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a lag is a delay, as in time lag

explanation.definitionFit: A festive occasion or special entertainment is a gala.

clue.text: One working half the time on tick?

definitions.text: One working half the time on tick?

parts.words: One working half the time on tick?
parts.note: a clock part that swings one way on the tick and back on the tock, so it works on tick only half the time

explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' looks like buying on credit, but it is the clock's sound: the swinging weight spends half its time on tick and half on tock.
explanation.definitionFit: A swinging weight regulating a clock goes one way for the tick and back for the tock.

clue.text: Personal hint

explanation.definitionFit: Close and private matters are this as an adjective; as a verb it means to suggest something indirectly.

clue.text: Valet said so to regard no one in the room

definitions.text: Valet said so to regard no one

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words the room, spanning both

parts.note: alludes to the saying that no man is a great figure to his own manservant, who sees his master's every weakness

explanation.surface: A manservant claims his employer thinks nothing of anyone present.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the proverb 'No man is a hero to his valet': the valet says he regards no one so. 'in' points into 'the room'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that a manservant, seeing his master's flaws, never looks on anyone as a great champion.

clue.text: Dedicated to farming — it's heaven

parts.note: pledged or vowed, so dedicated in the sense of promised
the land is the life of agriculture, as in working the land

explanation.surface: Someone devoted to agriculture finds it blissful.
explanation.walkthrough: The Promised Land is Canaan, given to the Israelites in the Bible, and by extension any paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical land pledged to Abraham's descendants is used figuratively for paradise or any longed-for place of bliss.

clue.text: Board 'here set passages with familiar quotation at start of exam

parts.note: landings are the level passages set between flights of stairs
a tag is a well-known quotation or saying

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word exam is taken

explanation.surface: An examining board set extracts from texts, with a well-known quotation at the start of the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like an examining body; it is the verb, to get on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing stage is a platform where passengers get on and off boats.

clue.text: Made a face before being taken outside

indicators.note: the word for taken goes around, so it sits outside the word for before

parts.note: led, as a prisoner is taken away
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Someone pulled a face just before being escorted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made a face' could be any grimace; here it is a sly sideways look.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a sly or lascivious look is to pull a particular kind of face.

clue.text: Dairy produce turns me insane

indicators.note: the word me turns round, so it is read backwards

parts.note: mental is a slang word for mad

explanation.surface: Someone complains that cheese and milk drive them mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns me insane' reads as a complaint, but 'turns' only flips the two letters of me. Emmental is the Swiss cheese with holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss cheese is a product of the dairy, made from cow's milk.

clue.text: Press for a royal fabric

parts.note: moire is watered silk, a fabric with a rippled sheen

explanation.surface: A campaign by the newspapers for a cloth fit for royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' here is a cupboard, not the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A press is an old word for a tall cupboard for clothes or linen, which is what an armoire is.

clue.text: Primate having small meal in France lacks this?

definitions.text: Primate having small meal in France lacks this?

indicators.note: having means holding, so the ape holds the other word inside it

parts.note: an ape is a primate
petit is French for small, as in petit déjeuner, the small French breakfast

explanation.surface: An ape that eats only a small French snack must have little hunger.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole, the clue says why an ape making do with a tiny French snack seems to lack hunger; petit déjeuner is French breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A desire for food is what someone eating a tiny meal seems to lack.

clue.text: Born to a single parent, that's a limitation

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Born to a single parent, that's a limitation (7)' for MAXIMUM: no parse found; MUM (parent) and I (single) fit but nothing in 'Born to a' gives MAX, and searches give no explanation
annotationWithheld.clue: Born to a single parent, that's a limitation

clue.text: A very soft, semi-liquescent material

parts.note: pp is pianissimo, the musical marking for very soft

indicators.note: semi means half, so the first half of liquescent is taken

explanation.walkthrough: 'semi-' takes LIQUE, the first half of LIQUESCENT (becoming liquid).
explanation.definitionFit: Appliqué is decorative needlework in which pieces of cloth are sewn onto a fabric.

clue.text: Unforeseen turn made awkwardly

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests clumsy handling, so the letters of turn made are jumbled

explanation.surface: An unexpected turn was executed clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never even imagined in a dream was not foreseen.

clue.text: Teacher on the job needs support for his retirement

parts.note: BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teacher's degree
a post is a job

explanation.surface: A working teacher needs a pension for when he stops work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' looks like the end of a career; it is going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedpost holds up the bed, where one goes on retiring for the night.

clue.text: Deeper: trouble engulfs soldier:" turning his back in the line

indicators.note: the stirred letters swallow the other piece, which ends up inside them
trouble suggests disturbance, so the letters of deeper are stirred up
the soldier turns round, so his word is read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: A deeper problem surrounds a soldier who deserts his comrades in the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges DEEPER to PEDREE, and 'turning his back' makes IG of the soldier; 'line' is ancestry, not a battle line.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedigree is a line of descent, a recorded ancestry.

clue.text: Cause irritation right on the joint

parts.note: the ankle is a joint of the leg

explanation.surface: A sore right foot is chafing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankles keeps annoying or galling a person.

clue.text: Each year, Jehovah requires a temple

parts.note: PA is per annum, Latin for each year
Jehovah is a name for God in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A god demands a temple be built for him every year.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower used as a Buddhist or Hindu temple in Asia.

clue.text: Crisis at the bus terminus?

explanation.definitionFit: A decisive moment of change is a crisis; and a terminus is literally where buses go round to head back.

clue.text: Old character will come quickly to the point

parts.note: to run is to come quickly
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: An old-timer will get straight to the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old character' looks like an aged person; it is a letter of an ancient alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Runes were letters of the ancient Germanic alphabet.

clue.text: Not present for this fixture

explanation.definitionFit: Absent from somewhere is not here; in sport a match played at the other side's ground is this kind of fixture.

clue.text: Good holder of drink — but he never got any

explanation.definitionFit: A tantalus is a locked stand for decanters; the Greek king of that name was punished with water that receded whenever he tried to drink.

clue.text: In retrospect, the inevitable outcome points to the 14th century

indicators.note: looking back means the word for a sure thing is read backwards

parts.note: a cert is a racing word for a certainty
E and N are two compass points, east and north

explanation.surface: Looking back, fate pointed to medieval times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In retrospect' reverses CERT to TREC; add EN and TO. Trecento is Italian for the 1300s in art.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian art history calls the 1300s by the word for three hundred, as in the period of Giotto.
